Entries.Text: Show the Tools window: Palette and Problems.
Deletes the selected block. A C-block goes with everything inside it, and a goto's closing label goes with it when nothing else jumps there.
EMEVD Editor: {0} was not done, it would add: {1}.

Double-click an instruction to insert it after the bottom selected block, or drag it onto the Script window: before a block, onto a C-block's foot for the end of that block, or onto the event header for the top. Its arguments start at their defaults.
The instruction layouts for this game didn't load.
Select an event to insert into.
Every instruction the game's layouts know, by class. Filter by name or by key, e.g. 2003[66].

The checks over every event of the selected file, run again whenever it changes. Click a problem to go to it. Vanilla files have a few of these too (gotos to labels they never define, calls passing fewer arguments than the event reads), so they aren't always mistakes. Block edits that would add one to an existing line are refused.
How many problems the selected file has, by kind.
Every problem, by event and line. Filter by event ID or problem kind.
The skip count runs past the last line of the event.
No label with this number comes after the goto.
An event parameter points at an instruction index the event doesn't have.
An event parameter writes at a byte that isn't the start of an argument, or past the instruction's arguments.
No layout decodes this instruction's bytes.
The Initialize Event passes fewer argument bytes (passed/needed) than the event it starts reads with its parameters.

Show skips and gotos as C-blocks holding the lines they jump over, with Else parts, and conditions just above the flow that evaluates them. Turn off to see every line flat, with every jump as a bracket in the margin. The file is the same either way.
Show each argument's name before its value in the blocks. Turn off to fit more values on a line.
EMEVD Editor: failed to read the instruction layouts {0}.
EMEVD Editor: failed to list the event files.
EMEVD Editor: failed to read the event names in {0}. The events are shown without names.
EMEVD Editor: failed to write {0}. It still has unsaved changes.
Write every event file with unsaved changes into the project folder, compressed as the game's file is. Files you haven't edited are left alone.
EMEVD Editor: '{0}' isn't a number. Type a whole number, or hex starting with 0x.
EMEVD Editor: {0} doesn't fit this argument ({1} to {2}).
EMEVD Editor: '{0}' isn't whole bytes of hex.
No layout decodes this instruction, so its bytes are edited directly. The length stays the same.
EMEVD Editor: the instruction has {0} bytes of arguments; type exactly that many.
What happens to the event when the player rests: keep running, restart from the top, or end.
This instruction jumps: changing its skip count or label changes which lines run. The brackets update as you edit.
Which of the event's start arguments writes this value when the event starts. With none, the value stored in the file is used.
Adds a slot after the event's last one. Every Initialize Event that starts this event must then pass a value for it, or the game reads past the arguments it was given.

The project's .emevd files. common holds the events that run everywhere, common_func the shared events other files start with Initialize Common Event, and each map file the events of that map. A file is read when first selected.
No .emevd files were found in the event folder.
The project has its own copy of this file.
The selected file's events, by ID. Names come from the .emeld beside the file, which only DS1, DS1R, BB and The Duskbloods ship. Filter by ID or name.
The file could not be read.

The selected event as blocks, one per instruction.
Click a value to edit it or link it to an event parameter. Drag a block to move it (a C-block moves with its body), or right-click it to copy, paste, duplicate, move or delete; Alt+Up/Down moves it, Ctrl+Z undoes, and Ctrl+S saves.
Ctrl+click adds or removes a block from the selection, Shift+click or Shift+Up/Down selects a range, and Ctrl+A selects the whole event; block edits and drags then act on every selected block.
Blue hexagons are conditions, orange blocks control flow, red blocks end the event, purple blocks start other events, and the other colours are commands by class.
A skip or goto that wraps whole blocks is a C-block holding the lines it jumps over (they run only when it doesn't jump), with an Else part when the body ends by jumping past one. A jump to the end of an enclosing block is marked as an exit. Conditions sit just above the wait, skip, end or goto that evaluates them, joined by a strip.
Jumps that don't nest keep a bracket on the left: skips orange, gotos blue, red when they run past the end of the event or miss their label.
Yellow pills are event parameters: the value comes from the arguments the event is started with.
Up/Down moves the selection, Enter or a double-click follows an Initialize Event, and Backspace goes back.

Block edits (move, copy, cut, duplicate, delete, drag) act on every selected line. A selected C-block takes its body with it, so lines inside it count once. The fields below are the line clicked last.
The end of this C-block. Drop a block here to add it at the end of the block.
Back to the event you jumped from (Backspace).
Instructions with no layout, or whose bytes fit none of its forms. They are shown as raw bytes. Vanilla files have none, so these come from mods or a layout gap.
Event parameters that point at no instruction, or at a byte that isn't the start of an argument. The game would write the value into the wrong place.

Skips that run past the end of the event, or gotos with no matching label after them. Shown as red brackets.
Vanilla files have some of these too (e.g. Elden Ring common event 715 jumps to label 1, which it never defines), so they aren't always mistakes; what the game does with them isn't confirmed.
The event header. Click to see its parameters in the Properties window.

{0}
No layout for this instruction: shown as raw bytes.
Double-click or press Enter to go to the event it starts.
The selected instruction's layout and arguments, or the event header's parameters when the header is selected.
Select an event or an instruction.
Each parameter copies bytes of the event's start arguments (slot X<offset>_<size>) over an argument of one instruction when the event starts.
Optional: some vanilla uses end before this argument.
Inferred: not in any shipped definition, worked out from the game's data.
Set by an event parameter when the event starts. The file holds {0} here.
Event {0} isn't in this file, common_func or common.
Another game's definition fits every vanilla use, and Bloodborne and The Duskbloods agree on it. Very likely right.
One other game's definition fits every vanilla use. The layout is proven by the data; the name is a suggestion, since the same ID can be a different instruction in another game.
The layout was built from how the game exe reads the arguments. It has no shipped name.
No definition fits: the layout was inferred from the vanilla data alone. It has no names.
